title: The Wrong Change at the Fish Market
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Every Saturday morning, I buy fish from the same stall at the wet market, mostly because the seller remembers exactly how I like it cleaned.
Narrator: Last week, however, something small happened that I have not stopped thinking about since, even though it lasted less than a minute.
Narrator: [carefully] The seller was rushing, because the queue behind me was long, and when she handed back my change, she counted too quickly.
Narrator: I did not realize the mistake until I was already walking away, and once I checked my pocket, I saw she had given me almost double what I was owed.
Narrator: [reflective] If I had simply kept walking, nobody would have noticed, and she would have blamed herself later, assuming she noticed at all.
Narrator: For a moment, I actually considered it, because this month has been tight, and that extra money would have covered my bus fare for a week.
Narrator: [honestly] Still, I turned around and walked back through the crowd, even though it meant losing my place near the front of the queue.
Narrator: When I explained the mistake, she looked surprised, and then almost embarrassed, as if she assumed most customers would have simply kept it without a second thought.
Narrator: [seriously] She tried to give me a small discount next time as a thank you, but I told her that wasn't necessary, and that returning it wasn't a favor to her.
Narrator: What struck me afterward was how ordinary it felt, even though the choice underneath it was not small at all.
Narrator: [gently] Nobody would have judged me for keeping it, and in fact, nobody would have even known there was a decision to make.
Narrator: That is exactly why it mattered to me, because the only witness to what I chose was the one I was doing it for in the first place.
Narrator: [encouraging] I still think about how easily I could have justified keeping it, telling myself it was her mistake, not mine, and that I deserved a little help this month.
Narrator: In spite of that temptation, I am glad I turned around, because some choices only matter precisely when no one is watching except yourself.

quiz.question: What mistake did the fish seller make?
options: She gave the narrator the wrong fish
She gave the narrator almost double the correct change
She forgot to clean the fish
quiz.explanation: The seller counted too quickly and gave back almost double what the narrator was actually owed.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator briefly consider keeping the extra money?
options: She wanted revenge on the seller
This month has been financially tight and the money would help
She thought the seller was rich
quiz.explanation: She admits the month has been financially tight and the extra money would have covered her bus fare.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do after realizing the mistake?
options: She kept walking and said nothing
She turned around and walked back to return the money
She left the money at the stall without explaining
quiz.explanation: She turned around and walked back through the crowd, even though it meant losing her place in the queue.

quiz.question: How did the seller react when the narrator explained the mistake?
options: She looked surprised and almost embarrassed
quiz.explanation: The seller looked surprised, and then almost embarrassed, assuming most customers would have kept the money.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator say the moment mattered to her?
options: Because she wanted to be praised publicly
Because the only witness to her choice was the one she was doing it for
quiz.explanation: She says the moment mattered because the only witness to her decision was the one she was doing it for in the first place.

quiz.question: Why must the excess change be returned?
options: It belongs to the seller even if she caused the error
quiz.explanation: Ownership does not depend on discovery.

quiz.question: What should the narrator not invent?
options: The seller’s income, family story, or need
quiz.explanation: Rights do not need a dramatic backstory.

quiz.question: What can identify the transaction?
options: Time, stall, amount, and a calm explanation

quiz.question: Why decline a reward?
options: Returning property is an obligation, not a favor owed a prize
quiz.explanation: Amanah is not performed for gain.

quiz.question: What is the quiet test in the story?
options: Choosing the owner’s right when no one may discover the error
